description: Live Preview: Gen 16 gripper (v016_generalist_rounded_point) can't close. The Open/Closed slider does nothing for it because the catalog serves Gen 16 as one merged OpenSCAD mesh named 'Gen 16' instead of the Left/Right finger STLs, so poses.js hinges (^Right/^Left) match no mesh. Cause: Scripts/publish_designs.py only uses viewer_parts.json STLs when they are newer than every dependency (mtime check); gripper.scad (09:48:15) was saved after exports/parts/*.stl (09:47:16), so it fell back to rendering gripper.scad whole. Also Gen 16 appears twice in catalog.json (same id) because cad/compare/designs.py adds any version folder with web/concept.js on top of the normal versions discovery. Fix: re-export the v016 parts (or make the freshness check robust to mtime order/git checkouts), dedupe catalog ids, and have a test fail when a posed gripper in poses.js publishes without its hinge parts. Verify in Live Preview that Gen 16 closes with the slider and Top view.

results.identified_issue: publish_entry's existing_valid used mtime >= newest dependency, which is fragile (save order, git checkout resets mtimes; STLs are gitignored). Rejected: content hashing exports against a re-render (costs an OpenSCAD run per part on every publish), and re-exporting on staleness (needs per-design part defines; export_models.py also rewrites tracked previews). Chosen: rows with declared_parts=True always use their parts and flag parts_older_than_source. Risk: real geometry edits without re-export now show stale parts until someone re-exports; that's surfaced in the flag, not in the UI. Dedupe: designs.py version-folder rows skipped in publish_designs.discover (designs.json and other designs.py consumers are unchanged). Verified: re-exported v016 viewer_left/right STLs were byte-identical; republished ~/HelpingHands-tools/design-gallery shows v016 ready with 2 models; Not verified in a browser.
results.summary: Gen 16 now publishes as its Left/Right fingers again, so the Open/Closed slider closes it; the duplicate Gen 16 is gone
results.detailed_description:
Cause confirmed as you described. Before changing anything I re-exported Gen 16's left and right viewer parts with OpenSCAD, and they came out byte-identical to the ones on disk. So the parts were never out of date. The publisher's mtime check simply saw gripper.scad saved a minute after the export and rendered the whole .scad as one merged mesh, and the slider's ^Left/^Right hinges had nothing to grab.

Fix in Scripts/publish_designs.py: any design whose parts are declared (viewer_parts.json, or the parts list from designs.py) now always publishes those parts, even when they're older than the source. When that happens the catalog entry gets parts_older_than_source: true, so the case shows up instead of silently falling back. This changes behavior on purpose: if someone edits a gripper's geometry and doesn't re-export, the gallery shows the previous parts (still movable) rather than a fresh but frozen merged mesh. A design with only a single exports/assembly.stl still re-renders when it's stale, as before.

Duplicate: the publisher now skips designs.py rows from <Project>/versions/ folders, because its own versions loop already lists them. Both copies had been writing into the same asset folder at once.

Tests (Scripts/test_publish_designs.py): one reproduces the exact Gen 16 setup (concept.js plus parts older than gripper.scad) and requires a single Gen 16 published as Left/Right fingers. The other walks the real repo and fails if any catalog id repeats, or if a gripper in poses.js would be served as a merged mesh or with parts its hinges don't match. I republished the local catalog: Gen 16 is ready with both fingers and there are no duplicate ids. The existing test_gripper_poses live-catalog check, which was failing on Gen 16 before the republish, now passes (14/14 OK). I didn't drag the slider in a browser myself, so please check Gen 16 closes with the slider and in Top view.

summary: Live Preview shows Gen 16 as one merged mesh instead of Left/Right finger STLs, so the Open/Closed slider can't close the gripper. Publishing should use the v016 part STLs, with a robust freshness check, deduped catalog ids, and a test failing when posed grippers lack hinge parts.
